newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses rise with record Dow, dlr stable.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses rise with record Dow, dlr stable.

text.p: European bourses were higher at midday on Friday, led by a second consecutive record close by U.S. blue chips after a solid U.S. 30-year bond auction and a stabilisation of the dollar after Thursday's sharp fall.
"The environment has cleared up, the 30-year T-bond has risen and the dollar, whose weakness weighed on the market on Thursday morning, is doing better," a French dealer said.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 28 points in New York to close at 6,206 on Thursday. The Dow was bolstered by good demand at the U.S. Treasury's bond sale, which helped push long-term interest rates down in the United States and Europe, and a strong earnings prediction from Intel Corp.

The dollar also recovered from its lows after the U.S. bond auction and remarks from Japanese officials. A Japanese economy minister said Japanese rates must be kept low for now, and a Japanese finance minister said he was not worried about the current foreign exchange market and the Japanese government should not intervene.
However, dealers said the dollar remained vulnerable.
"I think the dollar is likely to fall as far as 110.00 yen next week as a downward correction of the recent rally close to 115 yen," said a currency manager at a Japanese bank in Tokyo.
By 1200 GMT, the dollar was at 112.03 yen, up from 111.38 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
Germany's IBIS Dax index followed the Dow's lead, hitting a record high in pre-bourse electronic trading.

When bourse trading started, the Dax index of 30 leading shares also climbed more than a percent to a record high, with help from a jump in German government bond prices, implying lower long-term interest rates, and the slight dollar recovery.

Among some of the biggest gainers in the Dax was Dresdner Bank, Germany's third largest commercial bank. Dresdner shares soared more than three percent to a year high on news it plans to merge its global funds business.

Some dealers also saw Swiss shares within reach of a record high. Dealers speculated that if stocks could hold their positive bias, the SMI index could test its record high at 3,838.7 index points during the day.
In Paris, the blue-chip CAC-40 also got a lift, but dealers warned that gains could be limited before a three-day weekend.
On Monday, France and Belgium celebrate Armistice Day and the U.S. celebrates Veteran's Day.
Some dealers also said the CAC index needed to take a breather after recent gains to levels not seen in about two years before resuming its climb higher again.

Dutch shares were boosted by strong third-quarter earnings from Unilever. Unilever shares surged 12.50 guilders, or 4.85 percent, at the open after its third-quarter results reached the top of most analysts' expectations.
Unilever shares in London had soared about 50p by midday in Europe.
The rise in Dutch shares was also accelerated by some money mangers who, surprised by the market's strength, were forced to quickly buy shares so as not to miss the entire move up.
"Some people are having to pay up for stock they could have got a guilder cheaper yesterday," a Dutch dealer said.
Tentative stock index gains were made in Britiain, where inflation and interest rate fears kept markets on edge.

The Confederation of British Industry said in a report that October UK retail sales rose at the fastest rate somce 1988, which highlighted again the Bank of England's forecast on Wednesday that inflation and interest rates were set to rise.
"With inflation fears around, people are still scared this market will crack," said a senior equities dealer.
Further worries that could cap gains on London's blue-chip FTSE-100 stock index came from sterling's recent surge, prompting fears the strong currency will start to carve into corporate earnings.
By 1200 GMT, sterling was at $1.6479, little changed from $1.6481 in late European trading on Thursday.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5107 marks and 112.03 yen, compared with 1.5073 marks and 111.38 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 19.6 points higher at 3,920.00.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 5.41 at 2,217.22
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index rose 27.50 at 2,740.72.
PRECIOUS METALS
Morning gold fixed at $378.35 compared with Thursday's close of $379.45.
